faq: Do I own the plugin code?
Yes. When the order is complete you receive the full source and the right to use, change and sell it. We do not tie it to any licence from us.
Will the plugin keep working after WordPress updates?
We test on the current WordPress and PHP versions and write standard code that is built to survive updates. Future major changes may need small fixes, which our maintenance service can handle.
Can you list it in the WordPress plugin directory?
We can prepare it to the directory rules, but the review is done by the WordPress team and approval is not in our control. Many clients just use it privately.
What if a plugin already does this?
We check first and tell you honestly. Using an existing plugin is cheaper and often better, and we can configure it for you instead.

When no ready-made tool fits, a purpose-built one is cleaner than a stack of workarounds. Ecom Swift LLC handles custom WordPress plugin development, writing a plugin to WordPress coding standards, with a settings screen and a clean uninstall.

## What is custom WordPress plugin development?

A WordPress plugin is a package of code that adds a feature to a site without changing the theme or the core software. Custom plugin development means writing one for your exact need, such as a calculator, a special form, a data display or a connection to an outside service.

You receive an installable file and the source code, so the feature belongs to you.

## Why build instead of install

The plugin directory is large, and for many needs it has a good answer. When it does not, owners often combine several plugins to imitate one feature. That adds code that loads on every page, settings screens that overlap and updates that can clash.

A single plugin that does only what you need keeps the site lighter and easier to reason about. It also avoids paying for features you will never use, and it will not change direction because a vendor decided to.

## What good plugin work does for you

The main benefits are fit, speed and control. A plugin built for your process can save staff time, for example by turning a manual spreadsheet step into a form. A lean plugin loads only what it needs, so it adds less weight to pages.

Quality matters here because poorly written plugins are a common source of security problems. Code that cleans incoming data, checks permissions and removes its data when deleted protects your site and your visitors. Your outcome still depends on how clearly the feature is defined at the start.

## What a well-built plugin includes

- A written scope that states what the plugin does and does not do.
- Code that follows WordPress coding standards and naming rules.
- Safe handling of every input, with checks on who may use each action.
- A settings page in the dashboard, where the feature needs options.
- Custom database tables or fields, only when the data requires it.
- A clean uninstall that removes the plugin's data on request.
- Compatibility with your theme and the current WordPress release.
- Text prepared for translation, where multiple languages matter.
- A REST endpoint when an outside tool must send or receive data.
- Developer notes and a short user guide.

## How we build it

We begin with your description of the feature and write a scope that both sides agree on. That document protects you from surprises and protects the budget. We then build on a development copy of your site, test with your theme and share the result for review.

Basic covers a small single-purpose plugin, such as a shortcode. Standard adds a settings page and stored data. Premium includes a fuller feature set with front-end screens, an API endpoint and documentation. Add-ons cover an extra feature, a block for the editor and a separate security review.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the problem in plain words, with an example.
- Check whether an existing plugin already solves it.
- Launch with core functions only and extend the plugin in later releases.
- Test on a staging copy before the live site.
- Keep the source code and guide in a safe place.

**Avoid:**
- Putting custom code in the theme's functions file when it should live in a plugin.
- Requesting many features before the first one works.
- Installing the plugin on a live site without a backup.
- Leaving the plugin untested after major WordPress releases.
- Ignoring security notes from the review.

## Who it is for

Businesses with an unusual process, such as a custom quote calculator, often cannot find a ready-made answer. Agencies sometimes need a small tool for one client. Site owners who run a bloated setup of overlapping plugins may want a single clean replacement.

## How to get started

Send a short description of the feature, who will use it and where it appears on the site. Screenshots or examples of similar features are very useful. We never need passwords. We develop on a copy and install on your site through a collaborator or administrator user that you can remove afterwards. The code is yours on delivery.
